findings.title: A sighting on a joined member logs only the member; the head's names stay stale in the engine
findings.where: rust/crates/book/migrations/028-the-record-s-changes.sql:63 `SELECT 'instrument', k FROM (SELECT NEW.instrument_id AS k)` (and :146/:153 source_records, :76 instruments_described); rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:438 `WHERE s.instrument_id IN {} ORDER BY s.day` with group_sql(head) (:949 `UNION SELECT instrument_id FROM instrument_joins WHERE into_id = {param}`); rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:94 `book.instrument_as_read(*id)...`
findings.claim: `names(head)` reads the sightings of every instrument joined into the head. A sighting is written under the instrument its record's reference resolves to (identity.rs:609, the raw successor id), and the trigger logs only that id. `delta` then reads `instrument_as_read(member)`, which is None for a joined id, and never reads the head again. The head's InstrumentInfo.names in the engine (current symbol, name, last_seen of the run) differ from a whole read. This is the brief-26 condition that the log must name every key whose read changes, not only the row's own. The same applies when a record of the member is removed (the source_records and sighting triggers log the member) and to the instruments_described fallback, which also reads through group_sql.
findings.failing_scenario: Retired id A ("XYZ") and successor id B ("XYZ") are joined into A, the head because it was seen first. Later the company changes ticker and Wealthsimple rows for B carry "XYZW". Each pull stores records whose sightings go on B, and the log holds instrument B and the records. The engine re-reads the records (their transactions read as A), drops B (already absent), and keeps A's names ending in "XYZ". The page shows "XYZ" for the holding and its trades. A restart (a fresh build) shows "XYZW". `same_as_fresh`'s `ledger == engine_inputs::ledger(&book)` would fail, but no test writes a sighting on a joined member.
findings.required_change: Log the canonical head as well: in the sighting, listings_named, instruments_described and source_records triggers, also insert `COALESCE((SELECT into_id FROM instrument_joins WHERE instrument_id = X), X)`. Alternatively, have `delta` expand each instrument key to `canonical(id)`. Add a case to the server writer test (or the successions tests) that joins two ids, stores a record on the member with a new symbol, runs record_changed and asserts same_as_fresh.

verdicts.why: I couldn't refute this. A record of a joined member writes its sighting under the member's own id. The migration-028 triggers log only that id. `delta` reads `instrument_as_read(member)`, which returns None for a joined id, and nothing maps the key to its head. A full read builds the head's names from every sighting in its group, so the engine keeps the head's old symbol until a fresh build. A pull does not rewrite `instrument_joins` either: `settle_successions_again` returns early when `wanted == held`, so no join trigger logs the head as a side effect.
verdicts.evidence:
Checked on the branch (d8237f76):

1. Where the sighting is written. `rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:562`: `resolve_instrument_from` finds the id with `self.own_instrument(r)?`, which reads `instrument_refs` directly and returns the raw member id, not its head. At :608 `self.record_sighting(id, name, seen_by)?` passes that id on, and :939 writes `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO instrument_sightings(record_id, leg, instrument_id, ...)` with `id.to_string()`.

2. What the trigger logs. `028-the-record-s-changes.sql:62-64`, `instrument_sightings_changed_insert`: `SELECT 'instrument', k FROM (SELECT NEW.instrument_id AS k)`. That is only the member. The `source_records` triggers (:146, :153, :158) log `SELECT DISTINCT instrument_id ... FROM instrument_sightings WHERE record_id = ...`, again the raw member ids. The `instruments_described` and `listings_named` triggers log only `NEW/OLD.instrument_id` too. Only the `instrument_joins` triggers log both `instrument_id` and `into_id`.

3. How the log is read. `rust/crates/book/src/changes.rs` (`changes_since`): `"instrument" => out.instruments.insert(...)` parses the key and does no mapping to a head.

4. How the delta is read. `rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:93-95`: `book.instrument_as_read(*id)...; d.instruments.insert(*id, i);`. At `identity.rs:260`, `instrument_as_read` is false when `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM instrument_joins WHERE instrument_id = ?1)`, so the member reads as None and the engine drops a key that is already absent (`input.rs:475-478`). The head is never read again. `figures.rs:96-98` calls `engine_inputs::delta(book, &changes)` with nothing in between that adds heads.

5. What a full read does. `identity.rs:433-439`: `names(id)` takes `head = self.canonical(id)` and reads `WHERE s.instrument_id IN {group_sql("?1")}`, where `group_sql` (:949) is `(SELECT {param} UNION SELECT instrument_id FROM instrument_joins WHERE into_id = {param})`. So `ledger()` (`engine_inputs.rs:53`, `instrument_info` -> `book.names(i.id)`) gives the head A names that include B's new sighting. The incremental path keeps A's old names.

6. Joins are not rewritten on a pull. `identity.rs:780-781`: `let held = self.joined()?; if wanted == held { return Ok(Successions::default()); }`. A stable join therefore fires no `instrument_joins` trigger that would log A.

7. Test coverage. `rust/crates/server/src/tests_ledger_log.rs` contains no join or succession scenario that writes a sighting on a member and checks the result against a fresh build.

Failing scenario, which holds as stated: A (head, created first) and B are joined. A later pull stores a record whose reference resolves to B, with symbol "XYZW". The log holds 'record' R and 'instrument' B. The delta re-reads R and removes B (None). The engine's `ledger.instruments[A].names` still ends with "XYZ", while `engine_inputs::ledger(&book)` gives "XYZW". The same gap applies when a member's record is removed or its `instruments_described` row changes.

verdicts.why: Confirmed on the branch. A record on a joined member writes its sighting under the member's own id. The trigger logs only that member id. `delta` reads `instrument_as_read(member)`, which is None for a joined id, and nothing re-reads the head. Yet `names(head)` reads the sightings of every id in the group through `group_sql`, so the head's `InstrumentInfo.names` in the engine goes stale. A whole read differs. The finding's own ticker-change scenario is shaky: if the successor's row also carries a live standing with the new symbol, `settle_successions_again` stops matching the retired id's symbol and parts the join. The `instrument_joins` delete trigger then logs both ids, which heals it. The defect still holds in the ordinary case: after a succession, every new trade arrives on the successor (member) id. Each such record extends the head run's `last_seen`, or changes its name or venue_name, while the joins stay unchanged, so nothing logs the head. The divergence appears on every pull, with no rare trigger needed.
verdicts.evidence:
- **Sighting goes on the member.** identity.rs:563 `if let Some(id) = self.own_instrument(r)?` resolves to the raw id. identity.rs:603-604 `self.record_sighting(id, name, seen_by)?` writes the sighting under that raw id, not the canonical one.
- **Trigger logs only the member.** 028 migration:63 `SELECT 'instrument', k FROM (SELECT NEW.instrument_id AS k)`. There is no COALESCE to `into_id`. The source_records triggers at :146/:153 and instruments_described at :76 are the same.
- **Delta reads nothing for the member.** identity.rs:259 `instrument_as_read` returns false when `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM instrument_joins WHERE instrument_id = ?1)`. engine_inputs.rs:93-96 then inserts None for that id and never touches `canonical(id)`.
- **Log is not expanded anywhere.** changes.rs `changes_since` inserts the raw key. figures.rs:93-115 `catch_up_named` applies the delta as read. input.rs:475-479 `Ledger::apply` only inserts or removes the listed ids.
- **Head's names read the whole group.** identity.rs:433-438 `let head = self.canonical(id)?; ... WHERE s.instrument_id IN {} ... group_sql("?1")`. identity.rs:451-456 extends `last.last_seen = seen` and replaces `name`/`venue_name` from the newest sighting.
- **No incidental head refresh.** `settle_successions_again` rewrites instrument_joins only `if wanted != held` (identity.rs:782-787). A stable join writes nothing, so its triggers do not fire.
- **Failing scenario.** A (retired, head, created first) and B (successor) are joined. A pull stores a new trade row for B dated today with the same symbol. The ledger_changes rows are the record and instrument B. The engine keeps A's names with the old `last_seen`; a fresh `engine_inputs::ledger` gives today. `same_as_fresh` (figures.rs:661 `ledger == engine_inputs::ledger(&book)`) would fail. The page's names reload (figures.rs:519 `n.reload(..., named.instruments, ...)`) is also handed only B.
- **No test covers it.** None of the figures.rs `same_as_fresh` call sites stores a record on a joined member.

findings.title: A failed rebuild leaves the old engine with the log already dropped and the watermark moved
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:183-187 `held.applied.store(upto, ...); ... book.forget_changes(upto).map_err(err)?; settle_trades(book, &mut e, held, now)?;` and :265 `*engine = Some(built(&self.home, &book, &self.cache()?, &z.zone, now, &self.held())?);`
findings.claim: `built` publishes its watermark, replaces the movements index and deletes the log before settle_trades and reattach_carried_notes run, and before the caller installs the new engine. In `rebuild` (after Clear data) an error in any of those returns through `?` and leaves the previous engine in place. `applied` now points past every change up to the new build, and those rows are deleted. Nothing later re-reads them. Before this PR the next `pulled` compared the whole ledger and healed the engine; now catch_up applies only rows above the new watermark. A panic poisons the lock, which every caller recovers with into_inner, so the same applies.
findings.failing_scenario: The person clears records. Clear commits and the log is emptied. rebuild builds whole, stores applied = N, prunes, then settle_trades fails: an open_trade refused for an opening a concurrent pull just superseded, or a 30 s busy timeout on a trade write. The answer is "Clear failed", and the engine still holds every cleared record, trade and position. Every later change applies only its own delta on top, so the cleared rows stay in the figures until restart.
findings.required_change: Make `built` return the engine with its upto and have the caller store the watermark, swap the movements and drop the log only after the engine is installed. Or, on any error in rebuild, set `*engine = None`, so that the next state_zone builds whole. Test it with a forced failure in settle_trades during rebuild.

verdicts.why: The finding holds on the branch. `built` sets the watermark, replaces the movements index and deletes the change log before it calls settle_trades or reattach_carried_notes. `rebuild` then puts the result into `*engine` with `?`. So any error inside `built` (or in `self.cache()?` before it) leaves the old engine installed. Clear has already run `DELETE FROM ledger_changes`, and `built` has already moved `applied` up to the new upto. Nothing can now carry the cleared state into the old engine. `pulled` reads only `catch_up_named` (changes_since(applied)) and then settle_trades. Before this PR, `pulled` compared the whole ledger, trades, groups, journal and adjustments against the book and healed a stale engine. That safety net is gone, so this is a regression this PR introduced. No code sets `*engine = None` on an error. The trigger is rare: a SQLite error or busy timeout during settle_trades or reattach right after a successful Clear. When it happens, the cleared records stay in the figures until restart. Medium is the right severity.
verdicts.evidence:
rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:183-187 (`built`): `held.applied.store(upto, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst); *held.movements.lock()... = crate::csv_import::Movements::build(&e.inputs().ledger); book.forget_changes(upto).map_err(err)?; settle_trades(book, &mut e, held, now)?;` and then `reattach_carried_notes(...)?` / `catch_up(...)?`. All of these run before `Ok(e)`.
figures.rs:265 (`rebuild`): `*engine = Some(built(&self.home, &book, &self.cache()?, &z.zone, now, &self.held())?);`. On Err, the old Some(engine) is untouched and nothing sets it to None (grep finds `= None` only for `names`).
figures.rs:499-508 (`pulled`): only `catch_up_named(&book, e, &held)?` then `settle_trades`, with no comparison of the whole ledger.
Base d6824aa7 `pulled`: `if e.inputs().ledger != ledger { merge(&mut moved, e.apply(Change::Ledger(ledger))); }` plus whole comparisons of trades, groups, journal and adjustments. That code healed a stale engine on the next pull, and the branch removed it.
book/src/clear.rs:217: `c.execute("DELETE FROM ledger_changes", [])?;`. Clear empties the log, so the old engine cannot catch up on the cleared rows.
clear.rs:177: `f.rebuild(now).map_err(Refused::Failed)?;`. The caller only reports the failure. Scenario: Clear(Entries) commits, then rebuild's settle_trades hits a book error (for example a busy timeout on open_trade). Clear answers Failed, but the old engine still holds every cleared transaction and trade. Every later pull applies only rows above the new watermark, so the cleared positions stay in the figures until the server restarts.

verdicts.why:
The mechanism is real, and it is a regression from master. In `built` (figures.rs:181-192), `held.applied.store(upto)`, the movements swap and `book.forget_changes(upto)` all run before `settle_trades` and `reattach_carried_notes`. `rebuild` (figures.rs:265) assigns the engine only when `built` returns Ok. On any error after line 185, the old engine stays installed while `applied` points past the dropped log rows. `catch_up_named` (figures.rs:~92) reads only `changes_since(after)`, so the cleared rows are never applied to the old engine. `state_zone` builds whole only when the engine is None (figures.rs:443-444), and `pulled` returns early only when it is None. So nothing rebuilds until a restart or a successful retry of Clear.

On master d6824aa7, `pulled` compared the whole ledger, trades, groups, journal and adjustments read fresh from the book against the engine, so the next pull or record change healed it. That is no longer true.

I lower the severity from medium to low:
- It needs an error inside settle_trades or reattach_carried_notes during rebuild, such as a busy timeout or an I/O failure. `clear` refuses while a pull is syncing (clear.rs:146), which narrows the concurrent-pull trigger.
- The person sees "Clear failed", and clicking Clear again rebuilds whole and heals.
- `open` and the `state_zone` None path do not suffer: on failure the engine stays None or the server stops.

Still, after a failed Clear and no retry, the figures show records that are gone from the book until restart, so the finding stands.
verdicts.evidence:
figures.rs:181-192 on the branch:
`let (mut e, upto) = in_snapshot(...)?; held.applied.store(upto, ...); *held.movements.lock()... = Movements::build(...); book.forget_changes(upto).map_err(err)?; settle_trades(book, &mut e, held, now)?; if crate::legacy_import::reattach_carried_notes(home, book, &e, now)? { catch_up(...)?; settle_trades(...)?; } Ok(e)`

figures.rs:265, in rebuild: `*engine = Some(built(&self.home, &book, &self.cache()?, &z.zone, now, &self.held())?);`. On Err, `*engine` keeps the old Some(engine).

The watermark lives on Figures (`applied: AtomicI64`, figures.rs:~252) and is shared through `held()`, so the old engine now carries the new watermark.

`catch_up_named` reads `book.changes_since(after)` where `after = applied.load(...)`, so the rows at or below `upto` are gone (forgotten) and never read.

`pulled` (figures.rs:499+) only does `catch_up_named` and `settle_trades`, with no whole-ledger comparison. On master (d6824aa7, figures.rs:420-445), `pulled` read `engine_inputs::ledger(&book)` and applied Trades, Groups, Journal, Ledger and Adjustments whenever any differed, which healed a stale engine.

`state_zone` rebuilds only on `None => built(...)`.

Caller: clear.rs:177 `f.rebuild(now).map_err(Refused::Failed)?;`. It runs after `book.clear` has committed, and a retry of Clear calls rebuild again (whole build), which is the only in-session heal.

Scenario: Clear with Entries/Broker commits. In rebuild, built stores applied=N and forgets the log. settle_trades then hits a SQLITE_BUSY timeout on open_trade and returns Err. Clear answers Failed and the old engine still holds the cleared transactions. Later pulls apply only the deltas above N, so the cleared positions stay in the figures until restart.

findings.title: compare-figures drops log rows the running server has not applied
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/compare.rs:281-283 `let applied = std::sync::atomic::AtomicI64::new(book.changes_upto()...); ... crate::figures::settle_trades(&book, &mut engine, &crate::figures::Held { applied: &applied, movements: &movements }, at)?;` with figures.rs:113 `book.forget_changes(changes.upto)`
findings.claim: `forget_changes` deletes every row `seq <= upto`, not only the rows this reader read. compare opens the book folder it is given directly, not a copy. When its settle_trades writes anything, its catch_up deletes all earlier rows, including rows the server running on the same folder has not applied (compare's own rederive writes and anything a pull committed). The server's next catch_up reads sqlite_sequence as upto and moves its watermark past the deleted rows without their keys. The brief accepted other processes appending to the log, but not deleting from it.
findings.failing_scenario: `bagholder compare-figures old.db ~/.bagholder-rust` runs while the app runs, just after a pull committed records R the server has not caught up yet. compare's rederive or settle_trades writes and catch_up prunes up to its upto, R's rows included. The server never applies R, so its holding and trades are missing from the page until restart.
findings.required_change: Give compare a Held that never prunes (a flag on Held, or a catch_up variant without forget_changes). Alternatively, prune only at the server's start and within the server's own process. Or have compare work on a copy of the book folder.

verdicts.why: The mechanism is real. compare.rs:281-283 hands settle_trades a Held, and catch_up (figures.rs:111-114) calls `book.forget_changes(changes.upto)`, which runs `DELETE FROM ledger_changes WHERE seq <= ?1` (book/src/changes.rs:87-89) on whatever folder compare was given. But the failing scenario needs compare-figures to run on the live book folder while the app is running, and the tool's own contract already forbids that. The module doc predates this PR (compare.rs is not in the diff for that line) and says the book folder given "is written (its trades are opened), so it must be a copy too". Before this PR, compare also wrote to that folder through `repair_merged_successions`, `rederive` (lines 247-253) and settle_trades' trade opens. So pointing it at a running server's folder was already a use the tool refuses in writing, and the change log adds no new hazard to a supported use. Every recorded run of compare-figures in the plans uses copies: stage-2-engine.md:181 says "on copies of the person's databases", stage-3b-wealthsimple.md:252 uses `$TMPDIR/bh-3b/run8`, and statement-gaps.md:59 and filters-everywhere.md:54 say "On a copy of the owner's book". Brief 26 accepts other processes appending to the log. That covers the server's own CLI subcommands, such as pull-broker, which do not go through catch_up. Nothing on a supported path runs a second pruning reader. Within the server, only the one engine holder calls catch_up and `built`. Following the documented use, no figure is wrong and no change is lost.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/server/src/compare.rs:12-13 (unchanged by the PR): "Both databases are read from copies; the book folder given is written (its trades are opened), so it must be a copy too." The diff for compare.rs (d6824aa7..HEAD) changes only lines 278-283: the Held and `trades_ranked`. Before the PR, compare already wrote to the book folder at compare.rs:247-253 (`book.repair_merged_successions(...)`, `book.rederive(m, at)`) and in settle_trades (`book.open_trade`, `move_trade`, `orphan_*`). Pruning is figures.rs:113 `book.forget_changes(changes.upto)` → changes.rs:88 `DELETE FROM ledger_changes WHERE seq <= ?1`. The only callers that pass a Held are the server's figures.rs (built/catch_up) and compare.rs:283. Documented runs on copies: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md:181 "on copies of the person's databases"; stage-3b-wealthsimple.md:252 runs on `$TMPDIR/bh-3b/run8`; statement-gaps.md:59 and filters-everywhere.md:54 "On a copy of the owner's book". Brief 26 line 49 accepts "other processes appending to the log (the server's re-read is idempotent)". It says nothing about a second app running on the live folder.

verdicts.why: The mechanism is real: `forget_changes` deletes every row with `seq <= upto`, and compare's `settle_trades` → `catch_up` would prune the shared log if compare ran on a folder a live server is reading. But the failing scenario needs compare-figures to run on the live book folder, and the tool's own contract forbids that. The module doc says the book folder it is given is written and "must be a copy too". That was already true on master, where compare's `settle_trades` opened trades in the book it was given. So running it on `~/.bagholder-rust` while the app runs was already unsupported before this PR. In the server process, compare is the only caller of `settle_trades`/`forget_changes`. No other process (MCP, read-sources) prunes the log. The brief's acceptance of "other processes appending to the log" therefore never has to cover a pruning second process in supported use. A scenario that breaks a documented precondition gives no wrong figure in the build as designed. The suggested hardening (a non-pruning Held for compare) is a reasonable improvement, but it is not a correctness defect in this PR.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/server/src/compare.rs:12-13: "Both databases are read from copies; the book folder given is written (its trades are opened), so it must be a copy too." The diff d6824aa7..HEAD on compare.rs only swaps `settle_trades(&book, &mut engine, at)` for the Held form (lines 280-283). On master, compare already wrote trades into the folder it was given. `grep forget_changes|settle_trades` over rust/crates finds callers only at figures.rs:113, :186-190 and :508 (server) and compare.rs:283. book/src/changes.rs:87-89: `DELETE FROM ledger_changes WHERE seq <= ?1` confirms the pruning mechanism, but it is reached out-of-process only through compare, which is documented to run on a copy. Book::open_in (book/src/lib.rs:104) takes no folder lock, so the hazard exists only when that documented precondition is ignored.

findings.title: The new log DELETE inside catch_up can fail a pull after the engine applied it, skipping its statements and the page's update
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:112-114 `if !changes.is_empty() { book.forget_changes(changes.upto).map_err(err)?; }` reached from :507 `let (mut moved, named) = catch_up_named(&book, e, &held)?;`
findings.claim: Every catch_up with changes now writes to the book, holding the engine's write lock while it waits up to the 30 s busy timeout. If the DELETE errors, `pulled` returns Err after the engine has applied the delta and moved `applied`. It skips settle_trades, the `Change::Broker` statements read for `stated_for`, the names reload, `wake` and `self.moved(moved)`. The page is sent rows without the statements that go with them, the case `pulled` exists to prevent (decisions.md 2026-10-09), and the version is not bumped. Pruning is housekeeping; its failure should not fail the apply.
findings.failing_scenario: A pull stores records and reads cash statements for account X. Another connection holds the write lock past the busy timeout, or the disk is full. forget_changes returns SQLITE_BUSY or SQLITE_FULL. The engine holds the new rows, but X's broker statement is not applied and no page is told. The header shows a cash difference until the next pull for X.
findings.required_change: Make the prune best-effort: log and ignore its error, since the watermark already protects correctness. Or move it after the rest of `pulled`, outside the path that returns early.

verdicts.why:
The code does what the finding says. rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:107-114 applies the delta to the engine (`merge(&mut moved, engine.apply(Change::Ledger(delta)));`), then advances the watermark (`applied.store(changes.upto, ...)`), and only then runs `if !changes.is_empty() { book.forget_changes(changes.upto).map_err(err)?; }`. `pulled` (figures.rs:507) calls it with `let (mut moved, named) = catch_up_named(&book, e, &held)?;`. If the DELETE fails, `pulled` returns early. That skips settle_trades, the `Change::Broker` statements for `stated_for`, the names reload, `self.wake()` and `self.moved(moved)`. The Moved for a delta the engine already applied is then lost for good: the next catch_up reads `changes_since(applied)` past the stored watermark and finds nothing to report, so pages are not told about those figures until something else moves them or they are sent whole.

The DELETE is new in this PR. The diff adds it at figures.rs:113 and in `built` at :186. The base `pulled` read the ledger whole and did no write of its own except settle_trades. So before this PR, a pull whose rows needed no trade settled (a dividend, a cash movement) could not fail inside `pulled` on a write. Now every pull that logged a change does a write under the engine's write lock, through a pooled connection with a 30 s busy timeout (crates/sqlite/src/lib.rs:29).

Two things keep it low. First, the trigger is an environmental write failure right after the pull's own writes succeeded: another connection holding the write lock past 30 s, or a full disk. Second, the same failure shape already exists at base, because settle_trades' `book.open_trade(...)?` / `move_trade(...)?` also fail `pulled` after the engine applied the ledger. The watermark is stored before the prune, so correctness of later catch-ups is unaffected. A failed prune leaves only rows that a later prune removes. Making the prune best-effort (log and continue) loses nothing.
verdicts.evidence:
- **The prune runs after the apply.** figures.rs:107-115:
  ```
  merge(&mut moved, engine.apply(Change::Ledger(delta))); ...
  applied.store(changes.upto, SeqCst);
  if !changes.is_empty() { book.forget_changes(changes.upto).map_err(err)?; }
  ```
- **`pulled` returns early on that error.** figures.rs:507-525:
  ```
  let (mut moved, named) = catch_up_named(&book, e, &held)?;
  merge(&mut moved, settle_trades(&book, e, &held, now)?);
  ... e.apply(Change::Broker(a, now_stated)) ... n.reload(...) ... self.wake(); Ok(self.moved(moved))
  ```
  All of the second part is skipped on Err.
- **The prune is a plain write.** crates/book/src/changes.rs:87-89: `self.conn().execute("DELETE FROM ledger_changes WHERE seq <= ?1", ...)`, outside any snapshot.
- **The connection waits 30 s.** crates/sqlite/src/lib.rs:29: `conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30))?`, and `book()` opens a fresh pooled Book (figures.rs:274-275).
- **The DELETE is new to `pulled`.** `git diff d6824aa7..HEAD -- figures.rs` shows `+ book.forget_changes(changes.upto).map_err(err)?;` as added lines. Base `pulled` (d6824aa7 figures.rs:420-450) read the ledger whole and applied `Change::Ledger`, with no log prune.

findings.title: An account that loses its last holding of a reached instrument keeps a stale broker check
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/engine.rs:640-642 `for i in &reach.instruments { reach.accounts.extend(self.matched.held_by.get(i).into_iter().flatten().copied()); }`, which runs after `rematch_families` has replaced `held_by` (ledger.rs:2313 `self.held_by.retain(|i, _| !ins(i))`, then the fresh build is absorbed)
findings.claim: Which checks are recomputed is read from `held_by` after the replace. An account that held an instrument of the region before the change, and holds nothing of it after, is rechecked only if one of its own records is in the delta or its cash share changed. The figures move but the check does not.
findings.failing_scenario:
Account A buys 10 X. A's transfer-out of 10 X (record O) is linked to B's transfer-in of 10 that names no instrument (record I); the lots land in (B, X) through `link_of`'s `unwrap_or(instrument)`. B has no cash rows. B's broker statement says held {X: 10}, so the check agrees.

Record O is removed: `Change::Ledger` with `records {O: None}`, the delta by_change.rs's `delta_for` sends. `remove_record` drops the link, and I now does nothing (no instrument). A fresh build has no (B, X) units, so B's check shows a units difference: X, own 0 against the broker's 10.

Incrementally, `reach.accounts` is {A}: the gone transactions are A's, the touched shares are A's (B has none), and `held_by[X]` after the change is {A}. B's check keeps saying it agrees until a restart, or until a later change reaches B.

The same happens when a linked transfer-out is revised to quantity 0 (`apply` returns before `apply_transfer`, and the linked receiver is in `links_in`), for a receiver that names X and has no cash. by_change cannot see either case because it writes no broker statements.
findings.required_change: Collect, before `Matched::replace`, the accounts in `held_by` (or in `books`/`units` keys) of every instrument in the region, and recheck them together with the accounts after. Add broker statements (held units and cash) for every account to the by_change generator, and a transfer whose receiving side names no instrument, so a stale check fails the test.

verdicts.why: I could not refute this. After a change to the record, the accounts whose broker checks get recomputed are: the accounts of the gone and new transactions of the named records, `delta.accounts`, the accounts whose cash shares changed, and `held_by` of the reached instruments read after `Matched::replace`. No step adds an account that held an instrument of the region before the change but holds none of it after. The figures do diverge: a fresh build shows a units difference for B, and the incremental engine keeps B's old check that agrees with the broker. The server can also produce this delta. Deleting a record goes through `transfer_links` deletes, whose trigger logs both records, so that path is safe. Re-deriving a record is not: `records.rs` `derive` rewrites the record's transactions without touching `transfer_links`, so only O's record is logged. That happens when O's legs fail to resolve and its rows become empty, or when its quantity becomes 0. The engine's own test contract cannot catch this either, because by_change writes no broker statements.
verdicts.evidence:
The recheck set comes only from these lines in engine.rs:

- 616-618 `come`, plus `reach.accounts.extend(accounts.iter().copied())`, where `delta.accounts` is empty.
- 629 `reach.accounts.extend(cash_moved);`. - 640-642 `held_by` is read after `self.matched.replace`. ledger.rs:2313 `self.held_by.retain(|i, _| !ins(i));` drops the old entry and only the fresh `held_by` is absorbed, so B, now holding no X, is absent.

`rederive` rechecks only these accounts: engine.rs:893-895 `for a in &reach.accounts { self.recheck(*a, moved); }`. Rebuilding positions (engine.rs:851-865) does not trigger a recheck.

The check depends on `matched.units` for (B, X): equity.rs:164-166 reads `matched.units.range((*account, ...)).chain(b.held.keys())` and `units_on(*account, i, as_of)`. A fresh build therefore gives a Units difference of own 0 against the broker's 10, while the incremental engine keeps the old, agreeing check.

How the server produces the delta:
- book/src/records.rs:275 `DELETE FROM transactions WHERE record_id = ?` in `derive` rewrites O's rows, and only the transactions and source_records triggers fire for O. On a blocking resolution failure, `rows` is `Vec::new()` (records.rs:260-264).

verdicts.why:
I followed the cited path on the branch and nothing in it rechecks B. Every way into `reach.accounts` reads the state after the change. B's own check is never recomputed, while a full rebuild would show a units difference for X.

How each path behaves in the scenario:
- The gone and come transactions belong only to A, since `records` holds only O.
- `delta.accounts` is empty.
- `cash_moved` (`touched`) is empty. `match_over` only adds an account to `m.cash` for a transaction that has `t.cash`, so a B with no cash rows has no share in the old family or the new one.

`broker_checks` compares `matched.units_on(B, X)` (now 0) with `b.held[X]` (10). `recheck` is the only way an individual check gets updated. The only full recomputation is in `derive` (engine.rs:361), and that runs on Clock and Rates changes or a fresh `Engine::build` at startup. So B's stored check keeps saying it agrees until a restart or until some later change reaches B. B's position for X does move (X is in `reach.instruments`), so the figures and the check disagree on the same page. The tests do not catch this: by_change.rs never writes a broker statement (no `Broker` or `held` in that file).

After any change reaching X's family, `rederive` removes both rows and inserts E/X, then E/W before it: the page shows [E/W, E/X]. Because both rows map to `Entity::CashRow(E)`, `moved` also merges the two rows into one entry.
findings.required_change: Give cash rows a total order (break ties on instrument, then on the row's place in `stock_dividends`), or insert at `partition_point` after equal keys, as `Matched::replace`'s `put` does. Key `Entity::CashRow` by (id, instrument) so neither row is lost from the report.

verdicts.why:
The finding holds. `shown_order` compares only (day, at, id). A stock-dividend row takes its anchor's id and has `at: None`, so two stock-dividend legs of one adjustment produce rows with equal keys. `build_cashflow` uses a stable sort, so a fresh build keeps them in push order, which is leg order (X, then W). In `rederive`, `now` holds the rows in that same order. E/X goes in at Err(p). Then `binary_search_by` returns Ok(p) for E/W because it ties with E/X, and `insert(at, ..)` puts E/W in front of it. The engine now holds [E/W, E/X] where a fresh build holds [E/X, E/W]. The wire passes `figs.cash` through in index order (`c.rows.iter().map(|i| &figs.cash[*i])`), so the page shows the reversed order.

The finding's own trigger, a change reaching only X's family, is not quite exact. If only X is rederived and E is not in `reach.transactions`, E/X is re-inserted before the E/W already there, which is the correct order. The order comes out reversed when W's family is rederived, or both X and W are, or the anchor E is in reach, for example when the event row itself changes.

The `moved` claim is also correct. `diff` collects (Entity::CashRow(id), row) pairs into a BTreeMap, so the two rows collapse into one entry and the first row's change can go unreported. In practice the position or payer entries for the same instrument would usually move too, so the page still refreshes.

This code is new in this PR. Base d6824aa7 only ever did a full stable sort, so it had no way to reverse the rows. The adjustment legs are taken from stated facts with any number of legs (facts.rs:449), so two `from == to` legs with a cost are representable. The case is rare and only affects the display order of rows on the same day, so the severity stays low.

- **Equal keys.** Every stock-dividend row of one event gets the anchor as its id. The cash order only compares day, time and id, so two such rows sort as equal.

When `link` supersedes F by broker record B, only F's key is queued. B's other legs (an OPTIONS_MULTILEG order's second contract, a currency conversion's 'paid' leg, a corporate event's receive and cash legs; wealthsimple mapping.rs:526, :743-772, :685-715) sit under other keys, and B's new taken state never reaches them. Master's next whole pass resolves a file row there that was ambiguous because B was one of its candidates. The keyed pass never does, and in release nothing notices.

File X brings F2 (Buy 1 C2 @0.80 D): ambiguous over {B, B'} in both passes. File Y then brings F1 (Buy 1 C1 @1.20 D): queued keys {K1}, F1 is superseded by B, and the whole pass agrees on that step (F2 is filtered out of the compared ambiguities). On the next pull, master links F2 to B', since B is now taken. On the branch K2 is never queued, so F2 stays live: C2 is held as 3 units against the broker's 2 until something else touches K2. findings.required_change: When `link` supersedes, queue every key of the `to` records' transactions (and do the same wherever a supersede link is written). Alternatively, have the log name the `to` record (a `link_records` trigger), so `catch_up` queues all of its legs' keys. Add multi-leg broker records (two fill legs on two contracts; a conversion's two cash legs) to the linking generator.

verdicts.why: I could not refute this finding. When `link` supersedes a file row F with a broker record B, the change log records only F, and B's other legs are never re-queued. Nothing afterwards touches them: an unchanged pull writes nothing and a restart rebuilds Movements with nothing pending. findings.title: Queued keys live only in memory and are lost on an error, a restart or a rebuild; nothing ever runs the whole rule again
findings.where: csv_import.rs:428 `let keys = f.links_pending();` (taken before the pass; any `?` after it, e.g. `book.supersede(...).map_err(...)?` at the write loop, drops them); figures.rs:185 `*held.movements.lock()… = crate::csv_import::Movements::build(&e.inputs().ledger);` (nothing pending after a start, a Clear rebuild, or the first zone); csv_import.rs:433-435 returns `Ok(Linking::default())` where master returned Err("the figures are not built yet") with no engine
findings.claim: Master's pass was whole, so the next import or pull redid whatever one call missed. The keyed pass depends on every key surviving in the in-memory queue until a `link` completes. If the write loop fails partway, the remaining keys are gone. If the server stops between a write and its `link` (the in-app updater's restart, a crash), the keys are gone too, and a start queues none. The pass also reads file rows from the engine rather than from the book's live set. So a concurrent `link` (an import thread and the pull thread) can supersede a file row in the book first; this pass then calls `supersede` on a row no longer live, which is refused (links.rs:40-41 "is not live, so it cannot be linked"). The import fails and its other keys are dropped.
findings.failing_scenario: An import stores a file row F that the feed already reports once. `record_changed` queues F's key, and the server restarts (update) before `link` writes. After the start `Movements::build` queues nothing. Master would link F on the next pull; the branch leaves F live and counted twice (a deposit or dividend counted twice) until something touches its key.
findings.required_change: Put the taken keys back on any Err from `link`. In `built`, queue every key that holds a live file row, so the first `link` after a start or rebuild runs today's rule over them all. That also heals any keyed/whole divergence that a release build cannot detect.

verdicts.why: The finding holds. On the branch, linking only looks at keys held in an in-memory queue. Nothing re-queues a key after an error, a restart or a rebuild, and no whole pass runs outside tests (`whole_plan` at csv_import.rs:562 is test-only). Master ran the whole rule on every import and every pull, so the next call fixed whatever an earlier one missed. The finding's exact scenario is weaker than stated: in an import, `record_changed` and `link` run back to back on the same thread (csv_import.rs:278-279), so a restart landing between them is a tiny window. The same loss can happen in more realistic ways, listed in the evidence. I keep the severity at low: every path needs an error or a restart at the wrong moment, and the cost is a file row counted beside the broker's own row until its key is touched again.
verdicts.evidence:
1. Keys are taken before any fallible step. csv_import.rs:428 `let keys = f.links_pending();` uses `take_pending` (csv_import.rs:409 `std::mem::take(&mut self.pending)`). After that come `let book = f.book()?;`, the `taken` closure's errors propagated from `candidates`, and `book.supersede(...).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;` in the write loop. None of these puts the keys back.

2. Every build starts with an empty queue and drops unapplied changes. figures.rs:185 `*held.movements.lock()... = crate::csv_import::Movements::build(&e.inputs().ledger);`; `Movements::build` is documented "Every row of `ledger`, nothing pending". It is followed by `book.forget_changes(upto)`. So rows written to the book but never caught up before a start or `rebuild` are absorbed into the engine without being queued.

3. A concrete path: in broker_reads.rs a pull returns Err (`Err(e) => { end_steps(app); return Err(e.to_string()); }`) before `f.pulled(...)`. pull.rs has many `?` after `store_row` at line 228 (statements::run at 284, store_balances at 270, settle_successions at 383, and others), so the broker row B matching an imported file row F can be stored and the pull still fail. If the app then restarts (in-app update or quit) before the next successful pull, `built` absorbs B with nothing pending. The next pull sees B Unchanged, writes nothing and queues nothing, so `link` returns `Ok(Linking::default())` at csv_import.rs:434-435. F stays live beside B and is counted twice. Master's `link` (master csv_import.rs:323-353) reads `book.live_records(&csv::source())` whole on every pull and would link F there.

4. The PR's evidence for "Linking equal to today's" is the cfg(test) assertion inside `link` plus tests that plant a lost key. That shows a lost key goes unhealed; no test covers a restart or an Err after keys are taken.

5. The concurrent-supersede refusal (links.rs:40-41 "is not live, so it cannot be linked") is real. The same race existed on master, which also built candidates from the engine before superseding. The difference is that the branch also loses that call's remaining keys.

verdicts.why: I could not refute this. On the branch, `link` takes the pending keys out of the in-memory queue before it does anything that can fail, and nothing ever puts them back. No path in a release build runs the whole-ledger pass: `whole_plan` exists only under `#[cfg(test)]`. `built` (a start or a Clear rebuild) rebuilds the movement index with nothing pending. Master was self-healing. Its `link` read every live file record from the book on every import and every pull, so a pass that one call missed (an error, or a crash between the write and the link) was redone by the next pull. On the branch, a file row whose link was missed stays live, and its movement is counted twice, until some later write touches that same key. Neither the plan (§D) nor brief 26 addresses keys lost to an error or a restart. The scenario needs a crash or kill in the short window between `record_changed` and the end of `link`, or an Err inside `link`, so low severity is right. The concurrent-supersede sub-scenario is narrower than the finding states. For two links to overlap on one key, a third write (a pull storing a competing broker row) must add that key back between the first link's supersede and its `record_changed`. In that case the second link sees the file row live in the engine while `supersedes_from` already shows its first candidate taken in the book, so it supersedes a row that is no longer live and fails with "is not live". Its remaining keys are dropped. It is narrow, but possible. Master read the file rows from `book.live_records` instead, which shrank that window. The concurrency sub-claim is not needed: the restart and error paths alone hold.

findings.title: The test-build oracle runs inside the in-suite capacity import probe's measured window
findings.where: csv_import.rs:443-456 `#[cfg(test)] { … let whole = whole_plan(f); …`, and whole_plan :564-568 reads `live_records(&csv::source())`, `live_records(&SourceName::person())`, `superseding(&csv::source())` and scans the ledger once per file row; capacity.rs:657-667 `let m = mark(); crate::csv_import::import_from(...)` with global counters `bagholder_sqlite::work::steps()` and `allocs()` (:275-289); `test_every_operation_is_measured_and_the_growth_rule_judged` (capacity.rs:1061)
findings.claim: In test builds, every import probe's counted steps, allocations and bytes include the whole-book linking pass, which the release path no longer does. The in-suite growth test, which the PR cites as holding the boundary for import ("the in-suite capacity test fails if either grows with the book"), therefore passes while measuring an O(book) component. That shows it tolerates O(book) work of the oracle's size, so it cannot catch a release-path regression of that size. Its numbers also are not the release path's numbers.
findings.failing_scenario: Suppose a later change made the keyed pass read the file rows whole, about the work of `whole_plan`. The in-suite test already measures that much work inside the window and passes (growth (c+4x)/(c+x) < 2 while x < c/2 at SMALL), so it would still pass. Only the release-built CI Capacity run would see it.
findings.required_change: Exclude the oracle from measured probes: skip it while a probe window is open, or run the in-suite probes with the assertion disabled. Alternatively, state that the import boundary is held only by the release-built Capacity run.

verdicts.why: One part of the finding is true: in test builds, `link` runs the `#[cfg(test)]` oracle `whole_plan(f)` inside the import probe's measured window, so the in-suite counts are not the release path's counts. The conclusion drawn from that is wrong. Work that grows with the book cannot hide a growth regression. It can only push the ratio closer to failing. The probes' wall time is ignored in-suite, and the budget numbers come from the release-built CI run. So no figure is wrong and no regression gets through. The PR's claim ("the in-suite capacity test fails if either grows with the book") still holds; the oracle makes the test stricter, not looser.
verdicts.evidence:
Checked on the branch at d8237f76:
- csv_import.rs:443-447 runs `let whole = whole_plan(f);` under `#[cfg(test)]`, and `import_from` calls `link(f, now)` at csv_import.rs:279. capacity.rs:663-664 opens the window with `let m = mark(); crate::csv_import::import_from(...)`, so the oracle is inside it. That part is confirmed.
- What the oracle adds to the counts: `live_records` runs "SELECT id FROM source_records WHERE source = ? AND state = 'live'" (book/src/records.rs:742). The only index that includes `source` is `source_records_key ON source_records (COALESCE(connection_id, ''), source, source_key)`, with `source` second, so the query scans the whole table. Its SQLite steps grow with the book, about 4x by breadth. Its allocations are small and nearly fixed: about 20 CSV rows, plus a few vectors per row in `whole_candidates`.
- The growth rule (capacity.rs:795-800) fails when four/one >= GROWTH_LIMIT (2.0). Write the release-path counts as c1 at one size and c4 at four times, and the oracle as x then 4x. If c4/c1 >= 2, then (c4+4x)/(c1+x) >= (2c1+4x)/(c1+x) > 2, so a component that grows 4x never hides a failure. The finding's own scenario (a regression R≈x that grows with the book) shows this: without the oracle it fails once x >= c/2, from (c+4x)/(c+x); with the oracle it fails once x >= c/4, from (c+8x)/(c+2x). The oracle catches the regression sooner. Only a fixed oracle cost could dilute the ratio, and here that cost is a few small vectors, tiny next to an import's writes and figure rebuild.
- Wall time does not affect the in-suite verdict: the test keeps only verdict entries containing "grew" (`v.over.iter().filter(|o| o.contains("grew"))`, capacity.rs:1077). The test's doc comment says the budget is judged by the release-built CI job ("the budget itself ... is the CI job's"). That job runs without `cfg(test)`, so its numbers do not include the oracle.
- Import by depth is on `OVER_BUDGET` ("import", Pair::Depth, "#419"), so in-suite only import by breadth is held to the growth rule, and there the analysis above applies.

verdicts.why:
The facts are right, but the conclusion does not follow from them. In test builds `whole_plan` does run inside the Import probe's measured window. Its `live_records` calls scan the whole `source_records` table, because no index leads with `source`, so the measured steps do include an O(book) term. That term is added to both the small and the 4x measurement, which pushes the growth ratio toward GROWTH_LIMIT. So it can only make the in-suite test fail sooner; it cannot hide a regression.

Take the finding's own scenario: a release-path regression y about the oracle's size x. With the oracle in the window the ratio is (c+4x+4y)/(c+x+y), which at y=x is (c+8x)/(c+2x). Without the oracle it is (c+4y)/(c+y) = (c+4x)/(c+x). The first is the larger, so the oracle makes the test more sensitive, not less. That some O(book) work below the 2x limit passes is how the growth rule (`judge`, `r >= GROWTH_LIMIT`) is designed. It holds with or without the oracle. Taking the oracle out of the window, as the finding asks, would make the test more lenient, not stricter.

The PR's claim "the in-suite capacity test fails if either grows with the book" still holds. The test passes with the oracle's extra O(book) work included, so the release path, which does less, also stays under the limit. On "its numbers are not the release path's numbers": the in-suite test asserts only the growth verdict and reports no figures. The PR's table and owner's-book numbers come from the release-built CI run and from the owner's book copy, which run without `cfg(test)`. Nothing in the PR is contradicted, and no figure, change or page state is wrong.

So `e.inputs().market.closes.get(&p.instrument)` is None for every listing, `closes` is 0 for all of them, and the sort falls back to the symbol. `target()` for `Pair::Breadth` (capacity.rs:676 `Pair::Breadth => held.first().cloned()`) therefore takes the alphabetically first held share. I rebuilt the generator's rows independently. I wrote a scratch crate depending on `bagholder-wealthsimple::generated` at this commit, with the OWNER, ×4, SMALL and SMALL×4 sizes. - owner ×4 targets GAB, 24 rows (GA is not held there).
- SMALL targets GB, 5 rows.
- SMALL×4 targets GA, 12 rows.

The PR's own depth rows show add-trade and import cost grows with family depth (allocations 36,120 → 137,572 on the depth pair, listed as #420 and #419). findings.title: settle_trades' catch-up drains other writers' changes and throws their names away
findings.where: figures.rs:88-90 `fn catch_up(…) -> Result<Moved, String> { Ok(catch_up_named(book, engine, held)?.0) }`; figures.rs:173 `merge(&mut moved, catch_up(book, engine, held)?);`; figures.rs:507-521 `let (mut moved, named) = catch_up_named(&book, e, &held)?; merge(&mut moved, settle_trades(&book, e, &held, now)?); … n.reload(&book, e.inputs(), named.instruments, named.accounts)?;`
findings.claim: `catch_up` reads `changes_since(applied)`, which includes every commit by any writer, applies it, moves `applied` forward and drops it from the log. When it is called inside `settle_trades`, the instruments and accounts named by those rows are discarded. A pull's book writes do not take the engine lock, so they can commit between `pulled`'s first snapshot and settle_trades' snapshot. When that pull then calls `f.pulled`, `catch_up_named` finds nothing past `applied`, so `named` is empty and the names are never read again.

findings.title: A names cache filled before the engine is built stays empty, because nothing resets it any more
findings.where: figures.rs:398-399 `let n = self.read(|e| …Names::load(&book, e.inputs())).unwrap_or_else(|| Ok(Default::default()))?; *self.names.write()… = Some(n.clone());`; figures.rs:444-448 (state_zone builds the engine and leaves `names` alone); events.rs:482-483 `let Some(f) = self.app.figures.get() else { return }; let names = match f.names() {`; http/model.rs:92 `let names = f.names()…` before `f.read(...)`
findings.claim: `names()` stores an empty `Names` when the engine is not built yet. On master that healed, because every record change set `names = None` (master figures.rs:458). With keyed reload, only keys that a later change names are added. `state_zone`'s first build (`built`) marks the whole log as applied and does not reset `names`.
findings.failing_scenario: A book holding records but no zone yet: for example the first start after the carry from the earlier app (`legacy_import`), where the page has not stated its zone. The page's feed step or /model request reaches `f.names()` before `state_zone`. The cache is set to empty, the engine is then built, and every carried instrument and account has no broker id on the page (`security: ""`, no order ticket) until a restart.
findings.required_change: Do not cache names while the engine is unbuilt, and reset `names` wherever `built` replaces the engine (`state_zone`'s first build, as `rebuild` already does).

verdicts.why:
The mechanism is real. `names()` caches an empty `Names` when the engine is not built. `state_zone`'s first build does not clear that cache, while `rebuild` does. Master's unconditional reset in `pulled` used to heal it; the branch's `pulled` only reloads the keys a change names. So an empty cache filled before the first build lasts until restart or Clear data.

The trigger the finding names cannot happen in the normal page flow, though. `/api/events` awaits `state_zone` before `Feed::open`, so the feed step cannot run first. The page's every-trade read of `/api/figures/trades` waits for `book.data`. A book with no zone has never had a page connect, so the browser holds no copy of it; `book.data` arrives only with the stream's hello, after `state_zone`.

The defect is still reachable by other routes:
- **A failed first `state_zone`.** If the build fails (`self.cache()?` or `built(...)` errs), the stream pushes "refused", opens the Feed anyway, and the step reaches `f.names()` at events.rs:483 while the engine is unbuilt. The cache is set to empty. When a later connection's `state_zone` builds, the names stay empty.
- **Order activity before any page.** `readback::followed` calls `account_name`, which calls `order_accounts` and then `f.names()` on every recorded order event. On a first start after the carry from the earlier app (no zone yet), with working orders carried by `legacy_orders`, a read-back before the page connects empties the cache.

In either case the page shows empty broker ids and the ticket offers no accounts for the rest of the session. On master the next pull fixed it. This is a narrow regression, so not refuted, low severity, with the trigger corrected.

findings.title: Option 1 (resume the match from the family's state) is unsound unless the Matcher's state and the whole-family inputs are guarded
findings.where: ledger.rs:2287 `m.expire_before(inputs.clock.today);`; ledger.rs:1229 `if self.ended_on_record.contains(&(account, instrument)) { continue; }`; ledger.rs:2201-2205 `ended_on_record: txs.iter().filter(|t| matches!(t.kind, Kind::OptionExpiry | …))`; ledger.rs:2206-2217 `places` (max over every row); ledger.rs:665 `order_key` (day, bucket, occurred_at, record_rank, source_key, …)
findings.claim: The family's end state has already expired every contract before today, and several inputs are computed over all of the family's rows, whatever their date: `ended_on_record`, coin `places`, `event_groups`, `links_out`/`links_in`. 'Dated after the family's last row' is not enough on the same day: a row stating no time sorts in bucket 0 or 2, around rows that state one. Imports of an activity export are back-dated, so resuming does not help them. The gate's import probe imports rows dated `MADE_UP_TODAY` (:662), so the gate would go green while a real history import stays O(depth).
findings.failing_scenario: (a) Last row 1 Oct, a contract expires 5 Oct, today is 13 Oct, and a sale of the contract dated 3 Oct is added. Resumed from the end state, the expiry was already applied, so the sale lands 'beyond what was held'; a full match closes the lot on 3 Oct. (b) The broker's expiry row arrives dated after the last row. A full match skips the expiry by date (`ended_on_record`); a resumed match keeps the zero-price close it already made, plus the record's own close. (c) A coin row with finer places changes the rounding tolerance of every earlier row.
findings.required_change: If built: keep, per family, the `Matcher` state from before the final `expire_before`. Resume only for insertions whose every leg is placed strictly after the family's last place: a later trade_date, or the full `order_key` on the same day. On resume, run `expire_before(new day)`, apply, then `expire_before(today)`. Fall back to the whole family when a row is revised or removed, when a new row is an expiry, assignment or exercise or changes a coin's `places`, or when adjustments, transfer links to earlier rows, or terms change. Add a resumed-equals-full property case for each of these, and an import probe on the depth pair with back-dated rows.

verdicts.why: The finding is about a design the build does not contain. "Option 1" (resuming the match from the family's saved state) appears only in the PR body's "For the reviewer: depth" section. There it is one of three unbuilt options handed to the gate ("Which, if any, is the gate's call"). It is not a claim that the build does this or that it is sound. On d8237f76, `match_over` (ledger.rs:2161) is given the reached family's whole transaction list each time. It builds a fresh Matcher and walks every row from the start. It works out `ended_on_record`, `places`, `links_out`/`links_in` and `event_groups` from those rows. It calls `expire_before(inputs.clock.today)` once, at the end of that full walk (ledger.rs:2287). No Matcher state is kept between changes, so nothing is resumed. The finding's own required change starts "If built". None of scenarios (a) to (c) can happen in this build: a sale added on 3 Oct, a late expiry row and a coin row with finer places all trigger a full re-match of the family, so the result equals a full rebuild. The caveats are reasonable advice for whoever builds option 1, but they show no wrong figure, lost change, wrong page state or contradicted claim in this PR.

findings.title: A write under a joined member logs only the member; the head it is read as is never read again
findings.where: rust/crates/book/migrations/028-the-record-s-changes.sql:62-64 `CREATE TRIGGER instrument_sightings_changed_insert ... SELECT 'instrument', k FROM (SELECT NEW.instrument_id AS k)` (the same at :75-112 and :295-306 for instruments_described, listings_named, option_terms and instrument_refs, and :141 for source_records); rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:94 `book.instrument_as_read(*id)...`; book/src/identity.rs:257 `instrument_as_read` returns none for a joined id
findings.claim: Sightings, refs, option terms and the names fallbacks are kept under the instrument's own id (`resolve_instrument_from` gets it from `own_instrument`, and `record_sighting` stores it). The book reads them under the head through `group_sql` (`names`, `instrument_refs`, `option_terms`). The triggers log the member's id. `delta` reads the member as None, because it is joined, and never reads the head. So after a join, any record, ref or term arriving under the member's id leaves the engine's InstrumentInfo for the head, its symbol index entry and the page's broker-name cache different from a fresh build, until a restart.
findings.failing_scenario: Shown with a probe on a copy of the branch (book/tests/successions.rs fixtures). Store `buy` under OLD (CH, 'Charbone Hydrogen Corp') and `sell` under NEW (CH, 'Charbone Corp.'), so NEW is joined into the head. Then store a sale under NEW whose name is 'Charbone Renamed Inc.'. `book.names(head)` changes to 'Charbone Renamed Inc.', but `changes_since(before).instruments` is `{member}` only (assertion `the head whose names changed is not logged` fails). The server's catch_up then removes the already-absent member and keeps the head's old names. A fresh build differs, and `same_as_fresh`'s `ledger == engine_inputs::ledger(&book)` would fail. The same happens when the member's listing changes ticker: sightings under the new symbol on NEW leave `Engine::named` indexing the head under the old symbol. A trade typed as the new symbol is not found by `held_by_symbol`; it goes to `Traded::Named` and lands on a new instrument, splitting the holding. Removing a record sighted under the member leaves the removed sighting in the head's names. A new broker ref on the member leaves `Names.security[head]` stale.
findings.required_change: Have every member-keyed trigger also log the instrument the row is read as: `SELECT k UNION SELECT into_id FROM instrument_joins WHERE instrument_id = k`. Apply this to instrument_sightings, instrument_refs, option_terms, listings_named, instruments_described and the instruments source_records logs. Or have `delta` (or `changes_since`) expand each instrument key to `canonical(id)` as well. Add a case where a record, a ref and a removal arrive under a joined member after the join, checked by `same_as_fresh` (ledger, names cache, symbol index) and by the book-level log test.

verdicts.why: I could not refute this. Every link in the claimed chain is in the branch code. When a record is resolved, the sighting, ref and option terms are written under the instrument's own id. The triggers on those tables log only that own id. findings.title: What settle_trades' catch_up applies is never given to the names cache

findings.claim: `pulled` reloads names only for what its first catch_up named. The catch_ups inside `settle_trades` read every log row past `applied`, including rows other connections committed meanwhile. They apply those rows to the engine and delete them from the log, but discard the instruments and accounts named. Nothing reloads those names afterwards, so the names cache stays short until another change names the same key or the cache is dropped.
findings.failing_scenario: Thread A holds the engine lock in `pulled` for a record change that needs a trade, so settle_trades will write. After A's first snapshot, a pull on another thread commits a record with a new instrument I and its broker-security ref. A's settle_trades writes the trade, and its catch_up reads both A's trade rows and the pull's rows (instrument I). It applies them and forgets them. A then reloads names only for its first `named`. The pull's own `pulled` finds nothing past `applied`, so it reloads nothing. `Names.security` has no broker id for I, and the page cannot name I to the broker (no order on it) until a restart or a later change to I.
findings.required_change: Return `Named` from `settle_trades` (or have `catch_up` accumulate into one `Named` held for the whole `pulled` call) and reload the names for the union. Add a test that commits a new instrument from a second connection between the two catch_ups and compares the names with `Names::load`.

verdicts.why: The finding holds; I could not refute it. On d8237f76, `catch_up` is a wrapper that throws away the `Named` result. It is what `settle_trades` calls (figures.rs:173), and it still reads every change-log row past `applied`, applies it, and then calls `forget_changes`. `pulled` reloads names only from the `named` set returned by its first call (figures.rs:507 and :520). If another connection commits rows (for example a pull storing a new instrument and its broker-security ref) after `pulled`'s first snapshot and before a `settle_trades` pass that writes, those rows are applied and dropped from the log, but their instruments and accounts never reach `Names::reload`. When the pulling thread then gets into its own `pulled`, `changes_since(applied)` returns nothing, so `named` is empty and nothing is reloaded. The names cache is only cleared in `rebuild` (figures.rs:267), so the gap lasts until the next whole rebuild or restart, or until a later change names the same key. The race is reachable: `pull_now` writes the book with no engine lock and only calls `f.pulled` afterwards (broker_reads.rs:395-409). `record_changed` callers on other threads (entries, CSV import, order read-back, journal) take the engine write lock in `pulled` and can be inside `settle_trades` at that moment. The stale cache is read for orders, `names.security.get(id)?` in orders/ticket.rs:116, and for the page's `security` fields, `unwrap_or_default()` in wire/build.rs:204/244/365. A new instrument therefore shows an empty broker id and cannot be ordered. The by-key test (figures.rs:~663) checks names after sequential changes only, so it cannot catch this interleaving. Severity medium stands: it needs a race, but the result is a lasting difference from `Names::load` that nothing heals until a rebuild or restart.

I confirmed the finding by reading the branch at d8237f76. `catch_up` (rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:88-90) is `Ok(catch_up_named(book, engine, held)?.0)`, so it drops the `Named` part. Inside `catch_up_named`, every log row past `applied` is read in one snapshot, whichever connection committed it (`book.changes_since(after)`, :97). It then advances `applied` to `changes.upto` (:109) and deletes those rows (`book.forget_changes(changes.upto)`, :113). `settle_trades` calls this `catch_up` at :173, `merge(&mut moved, catch_up(book, engine, held)?);`, and returns only `Moved`. `pulled` reloads names only from its first call: `let (mut moved, named) = catch_up_named(&book, e, &held)?;` (:507) and `n.reload(&book, e.inputs(), named.instruments, named.accounts)?;` (:520).

The pull's rows do name the new instrument. In schema/v28.sql, triggers on `instrument_refs` insert, update and delete write `'instrument'` rows into `ledger_changes`, and `changes_since` (book/src/changes.rs:62-63) collects them into `instruments`.

A later `pulled` for the pull's own write finds nothing past `applied`, because those rows were already applied and deleted, so it reloads nothing.

The writers really are concurrent. Each thread opens its own `Book` connection. `pulled`/`record_changed` is called from broker_reads.rs:409/429 (pulls), entries.rs:255, csv_import.rs:278, orders/readback.rs:177 and journal writes. Each of them commits to the book before taking the engine lock.

So the scenario holds. Thread A holds the engine lock in `pulled`, and its first snapshot is already taken. A pull commits a new instrument I with its broker-security ref. A's `settle_trades` then writes, because identity has `needs_trade`, and its `catch_up` applies and deletes the pull's rows. A reloads names only for its own first `named`. `Names.security` stays without I's broker id until a restart or rebuild, or until a later write logs instrument I again. A `Names::load` of the same book would include I.

The race window is narrow: settle_trades must write in that window. The result, though, is a lasting wrong state, not a transient one, so medium is fair.

findings.title: Clear deletes the change log before the rebuild that makes that safe; a failure in between leaves the engine stale until a restart
findings.where: rust/crates/book/src/clear.rs:217 `c.execute("DELETE FROM ledger_changes", [])?;`; rust/crates/server/src/clear.rs:156-171 (`renew_id`, `clear_cache`, `clear_old_store`, `remove_dir_all(snapshots)`, `delete_session` each `return Err(...)`) before :177 `f.rebuild(now)`; also figures.rs:184-186 `held.applied.store(upto ...)` / `book.forget_changes(upto)` run before `settle_trades` can fail inside `built`
findings.claim: Once the clear commits, the log rows naming every cleared record are gone, and only `rebuild` brings the engine to the cleared book. Any error on the way to `rebuild` leaves the old engine in place: the next catch_up reads nothing past `applied` and moves `applied` to `sqlite_sequence`. Before this branch, the next pull re-read the ledger whole and the engine converged. The same holds inside `built` on a rebuild: `applied` is advanced and the log forgotten before `settle_trades` and reattach can fail, while `*engine = Some(built(..)?)` keeps the old engine on error.
findings.failing_scenario: Clear the broker's records while `snapshots/` cannot be removed (a permission error, or a file held open on Windows). `clear` returns `Refused::Failed` after `book.clear` has committed. The engine still holds every cleared trade and position, and every later pull or entry applies only new log rows. The page shows the cleared records until the app is restarted.
findings.required_change: Do not delete ledger_changes in `Book::clear`. `built` already takes everything up to its snapshot as applied and forgets it, so the delete is redundant. Or call `f.rebuild` on every exit path after `book.clear` (rebuild first, then the cache and file removals). In `built`, store `applied` and forget the log only once the engine is in place.

verdicts.why: The finding holds. The change log is emptied inside the clear's committed transaction, and only `Figures::rebuild` at the end of `server::clear` brings the engine to the cleared book. Several fallible steps sit between the two and return early: `renew_id`, `clear_cache`, `clear_old_store`, `remove_dir_all(snapshots)` and `delete_session`. After such an early return, every later write runs `catch_up` from `applied`. `catch_up` reads only `ledger_changes WHERE seq > after`, and those rows are gone. It then moves `applied` up to `sqlite_sequence`, so the cleared records are never removed from the engine. Nothing else rebuilds: `state_zone` calls `built` only when the engine is `None`, and the only other `rebuild` caller is a test. So the engine stays stale until a restart. On base d6824aa7, `pulled` re-read the ledger whole (`engine_inputs::ledger(&book)` then `Change::Ledger(ledger)`), so the next pull converged. On this branch it does not, which makes this a regression. The secondary point about `built` also holds, though it matters less: `applied` is stored and the log forgotten before `settle_trades`/`reattach` can fail, and on error `rebuild` keeps the old engine. Severity stays low because the main path needs a failure after the book is cleared, such as `snapshots/` held open on Windows, a permission error, or the cache or old store being busy. A retried Clear that succeeds still converges.

findings.title: compare-figures now deletes the change log of the book folder it is given

findings.claim: When compare's settle_trades writes a trade, its catch_up deletes every log row up to the current sequence. That includes rows its own rederive and repair wrote before `applied` was read, and rows a running server has not applied. The module documentation requires a copy of the book folder, and the brief accepted 'other processes appending to the log', but this process deletes rows instead of appending them.
findings.failing_scenario: compare-figures is run on a live data folder while the app runs. A pull has just stored a new buy (log rows N..M), and the server's `pulled` has not yet taken the lock. Compare's engine sees the buy, `open_trade` writes, and catch_up runs `forget_changes(≥M)`. The server's catch_up then reads nothing past its `applied` and moves `applied` to M. The buy is in the book but in no figure until a restart.
findings.required_change: Have compare apply with a `Held` that never forgets, for example a flag on `Held` or a catch_up variant without `forget_changes`. Or refuse a book folder held by a running app (`hold_home`).

verdicts.why: The mechanics are as described. compare.rs:281-283 seeds `applied` from `book.changes_upto()` and passes it to `settle_trades`. Once a pass writes a trade, its `catch_up` runs `book.forget_changes(changes.upto)` (figures.rs:113), which is `DELETE FROM ledger_changes WHERE seq <= ?1` (book/src/changes.rs:87-89). The failing scenario, though, only happens when compare-figures is run on the folder of a running app, and the tool's own contract forbids that. The module documentation says at compare.rs:11-13: "Both databases are read from copies; the book folder given is written (its trades are opened), so it must be a copy too." Every documented use runs it on a copy: stage-2-engine.md:181 ("on copies of the person's databases"), stage-3b-wealthsimple.md:252 (scratch `$TMPDIR/bh-3b/run8`), statement-gaps.md:59 and filters-everywhere.md:54 ("On a copy of the owner's book"). The tool already wrote to the folder it was given before this PR: `repair_merged_successions`, `rederive` under every mapping and `open_trade` all write the book. Running it on a live book was therefore already outside its contract, because it rewrites the records under a running server. The log deletion does not open a hazard that a supported use could reach. The brief's acceptance of "other processes appending to the log (the server's re-read is idempotent)" covers the supported readers that append, not a diagnostic tool run against its documented precondition. The harm in the scenario is also temporary: the buy stays in the book, and the next start builds the engine whole from the book, so no record is lost and no figure stays wrong. Under the default-refute rule, a scenario that needs a documented misuse of a developer-only CLI, and causes no persistent loss, is not a correctness defect of this PR.

items.item: Brief 26, 1: a succession's re-pointing is logged
items.evidence: Done: the instrument_joins INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers (028:114-137) log, for OLD and NEW, both instruments, every contract whose underlying_id is either, every record with a transaction on either, every trade whose anchor_instrument is either, and every adjustment with a leg from or to either. settle_successions rewrites the joins with DELETE plus INSERT (identity.rs:785-787), so both trigger sides fire. book/tests/successions.rs `a_join_and_a_part_log_every_record_trade_and_instrument_they_re_point` checks the buy, sell and event records, the anchored trade and all three instruments. items.item: Brief 26, 2: `seq` is AUTOINCREMENT

items.item: Brief 26, 3: one snapshot under the lock, watermark monotonic
items.evidence: Done: `pulled` now takes the engine's write lock first (figures.rs:501-502). `catch_up_named` reads `changes_since` and every keyed read inside one `Book::snapshot`, a DEFERRED transaction whose WAL snapshot starts at the first read, which is the log read (figures.rs:96-100, lib.rs:138-146). items.item: Brief 26, 11: every table the read derives from has a trigger, found by the authorizer
items.evidence: listings_named and instruments_described have INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers (028:75-99). work.rs adds `tables_read`, which collects `AuthAction::Read` from rusqlite's authorizer while statements are prepared. tests_ledger_log.rs runs `engine_inputs::ledger` and `book.adjustments()` (the source of facts().adjustments) on a connection opened inside the count, on a freshly migrated and seeded book.
