items.item: CTO question 2: the one-snapshot read in catch_up, settle_trades' writes, dropping the log as applied, other processes, Clear, the start's build
items.evidence: Sound: the snapshot covers the log, the counter and every keyed read. Rows another connection commits after the snapshot get a higher seq (one writer at a time, sequence advanced inside the writer's transaction), so `DELETE ... WHERE seq <= upto` never drops them. A rollback leaves neither rows nor counter. In catch_up the apply precedes the drop, so a drop never commits before its apply. A failed or panicking apply leaves `applied` and the log untouched, so the rows are re-read. If settle_trades fails after catch_up, its committed writes stay in the log for the next pass. Clear empties the log inside its own transaction and rebuild then builds whole under the lock. The start reads the build and `changes_upto` in one snapshot, so triggers firing during the build land above upto and are applied next time. Not sound: (a) `built` stores the watermark and drops the log before settle_trades and before the engine is installed, so a failed rebuild leaves the old engine with the log gone (finding 2). (b) `compare-figures` runs catch_up with its own watermark and drops rows the running server has not applied (finding 3). (c) A failure of the new DELETE in catch_up skips the pull's broker statements and the page's version bump (finding 4).

fine: Every trigger in 028 logs OLD keys on UPDATE and DELETE and NEW keys on INSERT and UPDATE, so an UPDATE of a key column (transactions.record_id, journal.trade_id/group_id, adjustments.applies_*, trade_group_members.group_id, instrument_joins.into_id) names both sides.

INSERT OR REPLACE paths with recursive_triggers off (no PRAGMA sets it): instrument_sightings has PK (record_id, leg, instrument_id), so the replaced row has the same instrument key. transfer_links (PK out_record, out_leg) replacing out->in_old with out->in_new logs out and in_new, and delta's links 'replace every link on those records', which drops out->in_old because it touches out.
The instruments_described and listings_named upserts are ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, so their UPDATE triggers fire.

mark_removed and supersede call clear_derived (which deletes transactions, problems, sightings and adjustments, firing their DELETE triggers) before set_state, so an adjustment whose own record leaves the live set is logged by its applies key.
adjustments_where maps leg instruments through `joined()`, and the instrument_joins triggers log those adjustments by from/to leg.

transactions_where reads the instrument as COALESCE(j.into_id, t.instrument_id); records on either side of a join are logged, and trades.anchor_instrument is set on every live-anchored trade (migration 002 backfill, open_trade, anchor_on, move_anchor).

successions_due: the triggers cover what settle_successions_again reads: security_standings, instrument_refs (own_instrument), instruments (kind, currency, created_at) and corporate-event transactions, including quantity or instrument updates, since the WHEN tests kind on OLD or NEW. instrument_joins is written only by settle and by Clear, which also deletes instruments and so bumps the counter. changed and settled move inside the same IMMEDIATE transaction. The initial (1, 0) makes the first settle after migration run. Clear keeps the row.
The standing upsert's `WHERE ... IS NOT excluded...` skips no-op rewrites without missing a real change.
changes_since parses every kind and fails on an unknown one. upto is the max of the rows seen and sqlite_sequence, both read in the same snapshot.

forget_changes cannot delete a row the snapshot did not see. With one writer at a time and sqlite_sequence advanced inside the writer's transaction, any seq <= the snapshot's counter belongs to a committed, visible row (or one already pruned).
A rolled-back write leaves no log row and does not advance the counter (book/tests/changes.rs); a write on a raw second connection is logged.
settle_trades' loop ends: open_trade, move_trade and orphan_* are guarded (trade_on, anchored_as), so a write that changes nothing does not fire a trigger, and `changes_upto == before` returns.

`built` reads the whole build and changes_upto in one DEFERRED snapshot. market()/facts()/ledger() do no writes inside it, so the transaction never tries to upgrade a stale snapshot (SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT).

rebuild and state_zone's first build now run under the engine's write lock, so the watermark is only written with the lock held, apart from Figures::open before the engine is published and compare's own Held.

The authorizer test opens its connection inside `tables_read`, so cached statements are prepared again. It asserts the seed reached trade_group_members, journal_tags, adjustment_legs, listings_named, instruments_described and instrument_joins, and it runs on a book built by migrations, so a later table rebuild that drops a trigger fails it.
The thread-local READING and NAMING in work.rs keep parallel tests from mixing what they count.

items.item: Brief 26 item 4: the equality test compares Matched and Identity; the generator writes broker statements, saved groups, successions, a leg-unstated row and a multi-leg record on uncoupled instruments
Brief 26 item 8: a record's legs order as one record
items.evidence:
`place_in_match` (ledger.rs:2146) ranks a leg by `record_rank` over `ledger.transactions.of_record(..)`. `match_over` keeps `by_record` whole for every record of the family (ledger.rs:2167, `or_insert_with(|| ledger.transactions.of_record(t.id.record).collect())`). The one-leg look-ahead tests the whole record's length (ledger.rs:2259, `by_record.get(&c.id.record).is_some_and(|l| l.len() == 1)`).

A one-day record is applied at its first leg even when that leg is in another family: the leg is walked past (ledger.rs:2175-2183, `walk.push(first)`) and only this family's legs are applied (`in_order` built from `mine`). Legs of one record cannot tie on place, because `order_key` includes the leg name, so the `min_by_key` choice of first leg is the whole match's first leg. The chosen option (the whole by-record map, iterating only the family's legs) is stated in the `match_over` doc. Case 12 of the generator exercises the brief's scenario: record rank 1 against the sale's rank 2 at one instant, and a V sale between the two legs.

items.item: Brief 26 item 9: a saved group is rebuilt when any member's trip is
items.evidence:
There is no trip-to-group index. Instead every group is rebuilt on every `rederive`: engine.rs:820-822 (`TradeKey::Group(_) => true`) together with `groups_shown` (trades.rs:340), which runs over every group in the book's order with `used`. Trips that enter or leave a group are found from the symmetric difference of the trips held before and after (engine.rs:816-819) and are rebuilt or dropped. Group members' trips come from the updated `identity.trip_of`.

The result is correct for the brief's scenario: G's P&L is redone, and X's trip is suppressed while G holds it. The work is O(groups) per change. Test coverage is thin: changes.rs adds one group of two trades, and by_change generates no trades or groups.

items.item: Brief 26 item 10: three coupling rules made exact (leg-unstated account family with record_problems; adjustment anchor plus legs; transfer joins instruments)
items.evidence:
(a) `waits_the_account` (families.rs:48) uses the same condition as `Matcher::apply` (instrument None, leg-unstated, not an event; `mv != Move::Event` is equivalent to `kind != CorporateEvent`). `neighbours` joins `Cash(account)` and every instrument the account holds (families.rs:210-213), and `reindex` keeps `whole` up to date from the gone and come transactions. Migration 028:169-180 makes the `record_problems` triggers log the record, so a problem change seeds that record's nodes.

(b) The anchor row's legs (`adjustments.get(&t.id)`, families.rs:199-202) and `named_by` (each leg's from and to, back to the anchor's node, :185-193) join the anchor's instrument with every leg's instrument, whatever the parent is.

(c) A link joins `node_of` of the other side (families.rs:204-207), which is the receiving transaction's own instrument, or its account's cash where it names none. That matches `link_of`'s `recv.instrument.unwrap_or(instrument)`.

I traced every `Matcher` write (books for a delivery's underlying, a transfer's destination, an event's to-leg, the taints) and each lands inside these couplings.

items.item: Brief 26 item 13: keyed collections keep every row and the order the page shows
items.evidence:
The lists stay vectors rather than becoming maps, so no row per transaction is lost. Fresh lists are sorted by `place_in_match` (`in_match_order`, ledger.rs:2401). Rows are put in place with `partition_point(|x| key(x) <= k)` (ledger.rs:2329), which keeps a transaction's rows in the order they were found. Order and contents are held by the `Matched` equality and by `matched == match_lots`.

Trades, positions and cash are sorted vectors with binary-search insertion (engine.rs:840-843, 856-860, 873-876). Their order is never compared by any test (see findings), and cash rows can tie (see findings). The status lists are now ordered by the transaction's place (an event's rows by the anchor's place) rather than by when the matcher produced them. That is the same day, but not always the same position as master.

items.item: CTO question 1: Matched::replace and Identity::replace attribute entries to the right region
items.evidence:
I found no entry attributed to the wrong region, and no entry that survives a replace it should not, as long as the families are exact (by_change compares them on every step).
- A transaction that moves family on revision: `seed()` runs both before and after `ledger.apply` (engine.rs:565, 614), so the old and new nodes are both in the region. `tx_in` (ledger.rs:2310) then removes the entry by the current node, or because the transaction is gone.
- Entries produced about another transaction: rows keyed by an anchor or an event leg (`Beyond`, `StockDividend`, `UnitsDisagree` with `instrument: from`) carry an instrument in the anchor's family (coupling 3).
- A transfer's receiving side: `consumed`, `open_lot(dest, dest_instr, &to)` and `cost_on_arrival` stay inside the family through coupling 4.
- `roles`, `waiting`, `unapplied` and `disagreements` are written only for the applied transaction, which is in the family. The walked-past first leg of another family is never applied.
- Dust and arrived rows carry their transaction and are removed by instrument.
- Merges and splits: the region is every node of every old family of the seeds, plus the old family of anything a coupling reaches (`regroup`'s `take`), and the new parts are a subset of the region. So every old entry is removed and every new one comes from a rematched family. Shares are dropped for `gone` families.
- `put` needs the retained rows sorted by the current place. A place changes only with its record's legs or source key, and that record is seeded.
- `Identity::replace` is sound because `rederive` widens `reach.instruments` to whole families (engine.rs:638). A trip's openings, the trades anchored on them, and the trips a `moved` trade can land on all sit in one family, so `trade_of`, `trip_of` and `moved` (by trip instrument) and `joined` and `unclaimed` (by the trade's instrument, or gone) never mix a set instrument with one outside it. Orphaned trades are removed but never produced by `identify_in`, so the result is consistent.

One attribution gap is outside `replace`: which broker checks get recomputed (finding 1).

fine: `match_over` (ledger.rs:2160-2300). `links_out`, `links_in`, `ended_on_record`, `places` and the event groups are built from the family's own transactions with the same meaning as the whole match. Anchors are taken in id order, as master's `adjustments.iter()` took them. Cash is summed only over the family's rows. A walked-past first leg is never applied, and its `expire_before` and `record_units` calls are harmless.

Running expiries per family gives the same result as the whole match: `expire_before` records units at the expiry date itself and the dirty set is cleared after each transaction, so a family's expiries land on the same days.

`Families::regroup` (families.rs:222-288). The region takes in the old family of every node a coupling reaches, the new parts are a subset of the region, and nodes that no longer exist are dropped as a fresh build drops them. `reindex` updates `contracts`, `whole` and `named_by` before regrouping, while the old `family_of` still names the old families.

`Engine::rematch_families`: shares for `gone` families are dropped and the new ones inserted, and touched accounts' cash is re-totalled. When a merge or split renames a family, both the old and new names are handled.
`Identity::replace` and `identify_in`, given that `reach.instruments` is widened to whole families (engine.rs:637-639). The trades and `Change::Closes` paths also use whole-family sets (the region).

`seed()` covers a record's nodes and its link partners both before and after `ledger.apply`, the old and new underlyings of an instrument's terms, and every instrument in a changed account. Adjustments seed their old and new legs plus the anchor's node.
Migration 028 triggers on `record_problems` and `transfer_links` log the record keys (both sides of a link), as coupling 5 and the delta's links need.

`rederive`'s trade rebuild: no trip is both kept and re-emitted. Kept means not in `instruments` and not in `trips`; re-emitted means in `trips` and not held by a group. Trips entering or leaving a group are caught by the symmetric difference of held trips.

`Matched::lots_of` through `held_by` reproduces master's per-trip lot gathering in the books' (account, instrument) order, because `place` and `trip_for` add each lot's instrument to `trip.instruments`.

by_change case 12 does exercise item 8's rank tie (record rank 1 against the sale's rank 2 at one instant) and the first-leg rule (a V sale between the two legs). V is coupled to nothing else in the generator, so the test is not vacuous.
`place_in_match` cannot tie two legs of one record (`order_key` includes the leg name), so the walked-past first leg is the whole match's first leg and no record is applied twice.

items.item: CTO question 3 / brief 26 item 13: keyed collections keep every row and the order the page shows
items.evidence: Every row is kept: the match's lists stay Vecs (ledger.rs:2401-2410 `in_match_order`, `replace` inserts each row with `partition_point(|x| key(x) <= k)`), so nothing is collapsed into a map. Trades, positions and cash rows stay sorted Vecs in their old comparators (trades.rs `shown_order`, cashflow.rs:55 `rows.sort_by(shown_order)`, positions in `matched.books` order), and a fresh build gives the same order as master. items.evidence: wire/build.rs:736 and :743 build BTreeMaps by transaction id, so the iteration order of ledger.transactions does not reach the wire there. The `Names` reload is keyed and has no order.

items.item: Identity lists (needs_trade, moved, unclaimed, joined)
items.evidence: `in_book_order` sorts needs_trade by TripKey, which equals master's iteration order over `matched.trips`. `moved` and `unclaimed` are sorted by Rank, which equals master's push order in `ledger.trades` (ORDER BY created_at, rowid, with Rank = (created_at, rowid)). `joined` is now sorted by (TradeId, TradeId) rather than pushed in trip order. It only drives `settle_trades` writes and is never displayed.

items.item: PR claim: 'The figures are unchanged (830 lines, ids removed)'
items.evidence: By the PR's own description, the comparison covers trades', holdings', cash rows' and checks' figures, run on master and on the branch against one copy of the book. That means two fresh builds. It cannot see the incremental insert path (where the cash-row tie reversal happens). It does not include the header's beyond sentences (where the within-day order changed). No script is in the repository or the scratchpad, so it cannot be checked whether the lines were compared in engine order or sorted.

fine: The match's own application order equals master's: `order_key` breaks ties by source key and by leg content, which includes the leg name. A remaining tie therefore has equal occurred_at, and `place_of` (account, trade_date, occurred_at, record, leg) then orders it the way master's SQL `ORDER BY t.account_id, t.trade_date, t.occurred_at, t.record_id, t.leg` did. UUIDs as bytes match lowercase hex text, Leg is a String, and NULL/None sort first on both sides.

Place order differs from master's SQL text order only for two transactions in one account, day and whole second where one carries fractional seconds. jiff's `...:00Z` against `...:00.5Z` sort oppositely as text and as Timestamp. No displayed list depends on that order: the match tie-break needs equal occurred_at, cash rows are re-sorted, and status/wire build maps.
`Ranked` trades and groups order by Rank (created_at text, rowid), the same as master's `ORDER BY created_at, rowid`, so `groups_shown`'s `used` rule runs in the same order.

`trades::shown_order` is total (unique TradeKey). The rederive insert for trades cannot double a key: `rebuilt` covers every group and every trip in `trips`, which includes `held_was` symmetric-difference `held`.

Positions: the key (account, instrument, direction) is unique, Direction's Ord is Long before Short, and the fresh path matches master's iteration of `matched.books`. `build_positions(Some(i))` via `held_by` yields accounts in BTreeSet order.
`Matched::lots_of` iterates (account, instrument) in sorted order, matching master's `open` map built over `matched.books`. Groups' lots are concatenated in the same trip order.

Merging family matches: `put` uses `partition_point(key <= k)`, so rows of one transaction keep the fresh match's order. Within-transaction rows always lie in one family: an event anchor's legs are coupled through the adjustment, and a multi-leg record's legs are different transactions with different keys.
Within-transaction row order in a fresh build: `sort_by_cached_key` is stable and keeps master's push order for rows of one transaction.

`Matched` lists (beyond, dust, arrived, stock_dividends, disagreements, unit_disagreements, unapplied) are compared in order by by_change.rs:249 (`== match_lots`) and by `match_disagrees`. Fresh and incremental agree on them.

Identity lists: needs_trade sorted matches master's TripKey iteration, so the book opens trades in the same order. moved and unclaimed are in Rank order as on master. joined is reordered, but only `settle_trades` writes read it.
views.rs sorts (`sorted_then`, a stable tie keeping the engine order) and the page's lookups by key (views.rs:433, :706) see the same engine order as master for trades and positions.
scope.rs `cashflow`: sums through `Partial::of` do not depend on order. `payer_rate` takes the max day from payments and excludes in_units rows, so stock-dividend order does not reach payers.

items.item: Brief 26, item 5: linking re-runs each file row's own rule over every key a change touched, before and after; removals and supersedes touch; file rows in ledger order; exclusion sets by key
items.evidence: Most of it is built. `catch_up_named` (figures.rs:101-107) collects `gone` (the engine's rows of every record the delta names, before apply) and the rows after apply, then calls `Movements::changed`, which queues the key of every row on both sides. A revision therefore queues its old and new key (5c). A removal (`source_records` UPDATE trigger, 028:144) queues the removed row's key (5b; covered by `an_ambiguity_a_removal_resolves_is_linked_by_the_next_pass`). A file row superseded by `link`, and a read-back fill superseded by `fills_give_way`, change the from-record's state, so their keys are queued too. `candidates` (csv_import.rs:493-555) runs master's predicates per key and sorts by `(class, place_of)`. `Place` is `(account, trade day, occurred_at, record, leg)` (input.rs:67), so the order is master's (fills, then movements, then cash moved, each in ledger order); feed tier comes before statement tier. `superseding` is now read by key (`book.supersedes_from(r, &file)`, cached per record, :440/:505-516). `live_records` is done differently: file and broker rows are told apart by `mapping.source` on the engine's ledger, which holds only live records (`engine_inputs::delta` maps a non-live record to None). Three gaps: (1) a record becoming *taken* (the `to` side of a supersede) queues none of its own keys, because `link_records` has no trigger and `supersede` writes only the from-records (finding 2); (2) the queue lives only in memory, is taken before the pass, and is dropped on an error, a restart or a rebuild (finding 3); (3) an import whose rows are all unchanged queues nothing, so its report no longer names rows still ambiguous (finding 1).

items.item: Brief 26, item 6: today's three match keys (fills; movements with three day pairings; cash moved with no kind and two day pairings; each broker row under each of its days)
items.evidence: `Movement` (csv_import.rs:343-347). `Fill(account, trade_date, instrument, kind, quantity)` keeps master's equality fields, and the price is still compared per pair (:525-532). `OnInstrument(account, kind, instrument, quantity, cash)` and `Cash(account, amount, currency)` leave the day out of the key entirely. Days are compared row to row with master's own closures: three pairings at :536 and two at :543. `Cash` carries no kind, so a file "withdrawal" still meets a feed TransferOut. Each row is indexed once, with no day, rather than once under each day. The key is coarser than the plan's, so its candidates are a superset that the same predicate then filters: linking stays correct by construction, including settle-day matches. `Dec` is `rust_decimal` with derived `Eq` and `Ord` (dec.rs:24), which agree numerically, so a BTreeMap lookup equals master's `==`. Cost, not correctness: one key spans every day, so a recurring identical amount (a biweekly 250.00 contribution, a constant monthly distribution) puts all its history under one key. Each pass that touches it does file rows × broker rows, plus one `supersedes_from` query per broker record.

items.item: Brief 26, item 7: an oracle test with today's whole pass
items.evidence: The oracle is literally master's code. `whole_candidates` (csv_import.rs:572-641) is master's `candidates` byte for byte, renamed and put behind `#[cfg(test)]`. `whole_plan` (:561-570) reads master's exclusion sets (`live_records` of the file and person sources, `superseding`). The one shared piece is `plan` (:466-487): master's loop with the `book.supersede` call moved out, otherwise identical, and the whole pass seeds `used` with `taken` as master did. The ledger order the oracle walks is the branch's new `Place` BTreeMap, but it matches master's `ORDER BY t.account_id, t.trade_date, t.occurred_at, t.record_id, t.leg`. The assertion (:429-433, :443-456) is compiled only under `cfg(test)`, which covers every test in this bin-only crate. A release build carries none of it: no cost, and also no detection. If the keyed and whole passes would disagree in release, the keyed result is written and nothing notices. With no whole pass left, nothing ever re-links: the queue is empty after every start (`Movements::build`, figures.rs:185). The assertion compares `linked` whole but `ambiguous` only for rows whose first leg's key was touched (:453-455), not 'the ambiguous set equal' that plan criterion 153 states. Generator coverage: `linking_by_what_changed…` writes cash moved only: CAD deposits, two amounts, days 11-04 and 11-05, feed-tier `ImportMapping` rows, statement rows, removals of broker rows. It has no fills, no movements on an instrument, no settle dates (so no settle-day pairing), no withdrawal against TransferOut (no kind-less cross-kind match), no revisions, no `fills_give_way` supersede, no prices at several places, no multi-leg broker records, no removal of a file row. Fills and dividends reach the assertion only through the fixed tests (`a_row_the_broker_already_reported…`, `a_dividend…`, `a_row_with_more_than_one…`, the capacity activity-export import).

items.item: Brief 26, item 7: count criterion reworded
items.evidence: The plan's criterion is reworded (docs/plans/stage-3-the-record-by-change.md:154): "Linking reads only the rows under the keys the operation touched. A test counts the rows `link` compares…". No such test exists on the branch: nothing counts the rows `link` compares (grep for `links_pending`/`Movements` finds only figures.rs and csv_import.rs, and the two new tests count nothing). The PR's acceptance list does not mention the criterion. The only indirect hold is the capacity import probe, whose 20 rows share one Fill key. That probe also runs the `cfg(test)` whole pass inside its measured window in the suite (finding 4).

fine: `whole_candidates` is master's `candidates` verbatim (same predicates, same tiers, same three loops); `plan` is master's loop with only the `supersede` write lifted out, and `whole_plan` seeds `used` with `taken` as master did. The keyed `plan(found, BTreeSet::new())` is equivalent because taken records are dropped while candidates are built.

The oracle and assertions are `#[cfg(test)]` only (csv_import.rs:429, :443, :561, :572); the server crate is bin-only, so every server test (including capacity probes and pulls) goes through them, and a release build carries none of it.

The keyed predicates equal master's per class: the Fill key holds master's equality fields with the price compared per pair at the file's places; OnInstrument and Cash compare days with master's exact closures (three pairings and two); `is_fill`/`is_movement`/`is_moved` are mutually exclusive and equal master's closures.
`supersedes_from` (links.rs:140-146) has the same semantics as master's `superseding(csv)` set membership, read per record with a per-pass cache.

File and broker rows told apart by `mapping.source` on the engine's ledger equal master's `live_records`-based sets, because the ledger holds only live records (`engine_inputs::delta` maps a non-live record to None).

Order: candidates are sorted by `(class, place_of)` with `Place = (account, trade day, occurred_at, record, leg)`, matching master's iteration (fills, movements, cash moved, each in ledger order) and master's SQL `ORDER BY t.account_id, t.trade_date, t.occurred_at, t.record_id, t.leg`.

The Movements index stays in step with the engine's ledger: both change only through `delta.records`, and `gone`/`come` are read from the engine under its write lock in `catch_up_named` (also reached from `settle_trades`). Lock order is engine, then movements, everywhere: `link` takes the movements mutex inside `f.read`, and `catch_up` holds the engine write lock. No deadlock.

Revisions queue both the old and the new key; removals (source_records UPDATE trigger) and file-row or read-back supersedes (from-record state change) queue their keys. `an_ambiguity_a_removal_resolves_is_linked_by_the_next_pass` exercises 5b.
`Dec` derives `Eq` and `Ord` over `rust_decimal`, so BTreeMap keys agree with master's `==` for 1 vs 1.0, and `Money` equality is (amount, currency) as in the key.

broker_reads.rs:422 call site is unchanged and still follows `f.pulled` (which catches up and queues the pull's keys). `fills_give_way` (:427) runs after `link` exactly as on master, and the keys it touches are queued for the next pass, as master's next whole pass would have caught them.
`import_from` calls `record_changed` before `link` (csv_import.rs:278-279), so an import's stored and revised rows are queued before the pass runs.

items.item: Brief 26, 12: the gate measures depth
items.evidence: Built in the CI job. capacity.rs:93-141 adds `Pair::Depth`, with `Size { deep: DEEPEST_ROWS * times / 2, ..OWNER }`. `DEEPEST_ROWS = 349` (:75). generated.rs:437-446 plants `deep` round trips on `shares.first()` (GA) in `invest.first()`. `target()` (:673) sends both probes to `deepest()` on that pair. `judge` and `OVER_BUDGET` work per (op, pair) (:183-195, :787-820). I ran the generator in a scratch crate: on the owner books GA has 358 rows at ×1 and 1,406 at ×4 (3.93×), and it is held at both sizes, so the CI depth pair does measure the deep listing. Two gaps. (a) It only works by luck. Every deep round trip sells everything, and the last one closes at `days-3`. GA is held only because, with seed 1, one ordinary GA trade stays open. When the deep listing is not held, `deepest()` quietly picks another listing. (b) The in-suite depth pair (`Size { deep: 20/80, ..SMALL }`, :1066) never measures depth. In those books GA has 40 and 160 rows but is held in neither, so both probes pick GG, the same 15-row listing at both sizes. Because both depth ops are listed, the test asserts nothing for them anyway.

items.item: Brief 26, 14: the boundary criterion is held by work counted
items.evidence: The brief allowed this route. Add-trade and import are off `OVER_BUDGET` for breadth, and `test_every_operation_is_measured_and_the_growth_rule_judged` (:1062) checks growth below 2× between SMALL and SMALL×4. I ran it at d8237f76 (scratch target dir): it passes in 35 s. But in test builds the import probe's window contains the whole-ledger linking oracle. `import_from` calls `link` (csv_import.rs:279), and `link` runs `#[cfg(test)] whole_plan(f)` (:429-456): `book.live_records(csv)`, `book.live_records(person)`, `book.superseding(csv)` (a join over every link row) and a quadratic scan of `ledger.transactions`. The test passes with that inside the window, so a whole read of that size cannot fail it at SMALL. Only `entries::enter` and `import_from` are in any window. A pull's handler (`broker_reads.rs:409` `f.pulled`, `:422` `link`, `successions_due`), `write_journal` and the scheduler (#508, acknowledged) are not. items.item: CTO question: the PR's three depth options
items.evidence: None is built; the PR leaves the choice to the gate. Assessed against the code. (1) Resuming the match from the family's state is sound only with strict guards. It must keep the `Matcher`'s state, not only `Matched`, taken before the final `expire_before(inputs.clock.today)` (ledger.rs:2287). It applies only to insertions placed strictly after the family's last place: a later trade_date, or the full `order_key` on the same day. It must fall back to the whole family when a new row changes `ended_on_record`, `places` for a coin, adjustments, a transfer link to an earlier row, or terms. (2) Rebuilding only the round trips whose content changed does not bend the growth on its own, because the match stays O(depth); it is the complement `rederive` needs once (1) exists. (3) Name runs kept as rows removes most of add-trade's SQLite steps (the PR's own estimate: about 41,000 of 46,063 at ×4), but must equal the fold in `Book::names`. Details under findings.

fine: capacity.rs `sized` (:303-305) multiplies accounts, instruments and trades with `deep: 0` (from OWNER). `Pair::Depth.size` multiplies only `deep`, keeping the owner's accounts, instruments and trades. Generated row counts: owner-deep GA 358 rows, owner-deep-x4 1,406 rows (3.93×), as brief 26, 12 asks.

`OVER_BUDGET` is per (op, pair) and `listed()` matches name and pair. `listed_disagree` fails an unlisted op that is over and a listed op that is within, so the list can only shrink. add-trade and import are off the list for breadth.

`judge`: the wall-time check applies only to Startup, AddTrade and Import, and the growth rule only to ops that answer one change. The ratio handles a zero baseline. `bytes read` is skipped where `/proc/self/io` is absent.
The probe's flag reaches the subprocess (`pair.flag()` → `--depth` → `Pair::Depth` in `cli`). `measure` passes the pair through.
The fsync in `copy_folder` is applied to every copied file, the WAL included, before the timed exec. The startup probe is still timed from the exec.
The Pi column equals ×4 runner ms × 2.1 on every row. The brokers budget is 2,586 = `BALANCES_EVERY` ÷ 116 accounts.

The names reload runs in `pulled` under the engine lock, by key (`instrument_refs` / `account_refs` per named id), inside both probes' windows (cache primed before `mark()`). Migration 028 has INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE triggers on instrument_refs and account_refs.

`entries::enter` → `book.enter` → `record_changed` → `pulled` (`catch_up_named` by key, `settle_trades`, names reload) are all inside the add-trade window. `import_from` → `record_changed` → `link` (keyed `candidates`) are inside the import window.
`held_by_symbol` and `contract_by_terms` now look instruments up by index (`e.named`, `e.contracts_on`), and `transaction` by key, with no scan of every instrument.
The in-suite capacity test passes at d8237f76 (I ran it with a scratch target dir: 1 passed, 35 s).

Option 3 (name runs kept as rows) is sound if it equals the fold in `Book::names` (identity.rs:433-474): runs over `instrument_sightings` of the whole canonical group, joined to live records, where the latest sighting's words, `last_seen` and source stand for the run, falling back to `instruments_described` when no run exists. It must be maintained on a back-dated sighting splitting a run, on `source_records.state` changes (supersede or remove without deleting the sighting), and on `instrument_joins` join or part, and held equal to the fold by the by-change property test. It is the bigger lever for steps (the PR's estimate: about 41,000 of add-trade's 46,063 steps at ×4). I would require it now, together with option 1 for add-trade under the guards above (add-trade is over its RAIL budget at ×4 depth). Option 2 is required only as the complement to option 1 (`rederive` rebuilds every trip of each reached instrument, `trips_of`); on its own it leaves the match O(depth).

items.item: CTO: can a whole build at a start miss a write committed between the build's read and the watermark read?

items.item: CTO: the symbol index for entries (held_by_symbol, contract_by_terms, current_symbol)
items.evidence: `Engine::named` and `contracts_on` are kept from the instruments delta, and the engine moves an instrument out of its old (symbol, currency) key before inserting the new one (engine.rs:594-617). Covered: a renamed listing that is not joined (the sighting logs its instrument); an instrument whose only sighting is removed (the source_records update and sighting delete triggers log it, `instrument_as_read` keeps it, `names` falls back); a join (both sides and the contracts on them are logged). `Book::current_symbol` reads through the group and is held equal to `names().last()` by two tests. items.item: CTO: the names cache by key for an account and an instrument after a succession
items.evidence: At the join itself both ids are logged. `reload` removes the member (no longer in `inputs.ledger.instruments`) and reads the head's `instrument_refs` through the group, which matches `Names::load`. Accounts are re-read on account_refs, accounts and broker_connections changes. Not covered: a ref added to the member after the join logs only the member, so the head is not reloaded (finding 1). fine: `changes_upto` reads `sqlite_sequence` inside the same snapshot as the whole build (figures.rs:183) and as the keyed delta (:96-100), so a commit between the two reads cannot be skipped. In WAL the sequence order is the commit order, and `forget_changes` deletes only rows ≤ the `upto` that was read.

`Book::snapshot` (lib.rs) is a deferred read transaction on the connection's first read. `Figures::book()` opens a fresh connection per call, so a snapshot never joins another thread's transaction. Every call `build` and `delta` make is a read, so nothing upgrades the snapshot.

`pulled` takes the engine's write lock before it reads anything, so every read a pull applies is newer than what an earlier holder applied. `Change::Ledger` is applied at a single site (figures.rs:106), so no read made outside the lock is applied.

settle_trades writes only on the anchor the engine saw (`seen` from the engine's trades). It reads its own writes back through the log and stops when `sqlite_sequence` did not move, so it ends where the old trades comparison ended.

The instrument_joins triggers (028:114-137) log, for both OLD and NEW, the records, trades, contracts (by underlying) and adjustments (by legs' from/to) that `transactions`, `trades`, `option_terms` and the adjustments read through the join. `settle_successions_again` joins every member directly into the head, so no chain is missed.

`successions_due`: its triggers cover everything `settle_successions_again` reads (security_standings, instrument_refs, instruments, corporate-event transactions). instrument_joins is written only by settle itself, by Clear (together with instrument deletes, which bump the counter) and by the repair (through instrument_refs, which bumps it). `settled` is set to the `changed` read inside the same IMMEDIATE transaction, and an unchanged standing no longer rewrites its row (the ON CONFLICT ... WHERE).

Migration 028 backfills nothing, so no trigger logs the existing rows. `successions_due` starts due, so the first settle runs whole. v28.sql carries the same indexes and triggers (75 triggers; 027 had none).

The instrument as read by `delta`: `instrument_as_read` (exists and not joined) matches `Book::instruments()`, and a joined member reads as gone. A removed record logs the instruments it sighted (source_records update trigger, and the sightings delete trigger).

The engine's symbol index moves an instrument from its old (symbol, currency) key to its new one on each instrument delta (engine.rs:594-617). `contract_by_terms` reads `contracts_on(u)` and then filters on the terms, as before.

`Names::reload` removes and re-reads exactly the keys it is given, and skips instruments and accounts the engine no longer holds, so it matches `Names::load` for the keys it sees. `rebuild` and the build at a start drop the cache.

The authorizer-based test (tests_ledger_log.rs) prepares every statement on a connection opened inside the count, on a seeded book that reaches groups, journal tags, adjustment legs, listings_named, instruments_described and instrument_joins.

demo-facts writes through its own connection without opening the figures, so its writes (e.g. `UPDATE option_terms`) are logged and left for the server. The capacity builder opens the figures on a home of its own. `hold_home` keeps a second app off one data folder.

Clear keeps the sequence going past the cleared log (`a_clear_empties_the_log_and_the_sequence_goes_on`). `successions_due` is kept, and is consistent after the clear's own settle. A concurrent pull is refused while Clear runs (`Refused::Pulling`).
